exercises.name: Lateral Cone Jump
instructions: Stand just beside a low cone with feet hip-width apart, shoulders down and midsection braced.
Sit the hips back into a short quarter squat with the chest lifted and the back flat.
Without pausing, jump up and sideways over the cone with both feet leaving and staying level together.
Land softly on the middle of both feet, let the hips drop back to absorb the landing, then jump back the other way.
exercises.commonMistakes: Landing stiff-legged with the knees caving in, or rushing reps before each landing is under control.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hop side to side over a line on the floor and pause to reset between each hop.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains you to produce and absorb force sideways, which straight-ahead jumping never covers.

exercises.name: Lateral Bound
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, hip abductors and adductors, quads, calves
instructions: Stand with feet close together, knees and hips slightly bent, and lift one foot just off the floor.
Push off the standing leg and jump as far to the side as you can control.
Land on the opposite foot with the knee bent and the other foot held off the ground.
Hold the landing for a moment until you are steady, then bound back the other way.
exercises.formCue: Stick the landing before you go again.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the landing knee collapse inward, or bouncing straight out of a landing you never controlled.
exercises.beginnerModification: Shorten the distance and tap the trailing foot down for balance on each landing.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Single-leg landings build the hip control that protects knees when you change direction.

exercises.name: Battle Rope Alternating Wave
exercises.musclesWorked: Shoulders, forearms, upper back, core, legs
instructions: Face the anchor holding one rope end in each hand, feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent and back straight.
Lean the torso slightly forward from the hips and brace the midsection.
Raise one hand to about shoulder height while the other drops to waist height, then switch quickly.
Keep the arms trading places at a steady rhythm so each wave travels the full length of the rope.
exercises.commonMistakes: Standing bolt upright with locked knees, or letting the waves shrink as the arms tire instead of ending the interval.
exercises.beginnerModification: Step closer to the anchor for more slack, make smaller waves and work in 10 to 15 second bursts.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It drives the heart rate up hard with almost no impact on the legs.

exercises.name: Battle Rope Double Wave
instructions: Face the anchor with one rope end in each hand, feet shoulder-width apart, knees soft and back straight.
Lean slightly forward from the hips and brace the midsection.
Lift both hands together to about shoulder height, then drive them down to waist height.
Repeat at a quick, even tempo so both ropes ripple to the anchor side by side.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rounding the lower back to chase bigger waves, or shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a shorter or thinner rope and keep the waves small and rhythmic.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Moving both arms together loads the trunk and hips more than the alternating version.

exercises.name: Battle Rope Slam
instructions: Face the anchor with a rope end in each hand, feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Lift both rope ends up to head height or just above, rising tall through the hips.
Drive both arms down hard and fast so the rope hits the floor in front of you, letting the hips sit back as it lands.
Stand tall again and repeat with full effort on every rep.
exercises.commonMistakes: Slamming with the arms only and no hip action, or rounding the back at the bottom of each rep.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lift the rope only to chest height and slam at about half effort until the rhythm feels natural.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A full-body power effort you can repeat at top intensity without a hard landing.

exercises.name: Air Bike Sprint
instructions: Set the seat so your knee keeps a slight bend at the bottom of the pedal stroke, then pedal easily for a few minutes to warm up.
Start the interval by pushing and pulling the handles while driving the pedals, building to full effort within a few strokes.
Hold that effort for the whole interval, usually 10 to 30 seconds, keeping the pedal stroke smooth.
Spin very lightly through the rest period before the next sprint.
exercises.formCue: Push and pull the handles, legs follow.
exercises.commonMistakes: Going so hard on the first sprint that the remaining rounds collapse, or bouncing in the saddle with a choppy stroke.
exercises.beginnerModification: Work at a hard but repeatable effort for 15 seconds and rest for 45 seconds.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Resistance rises with your effort, so it delivers true sprint work with no impact.

exercises.name: SkiErg Double-Pole
instructions: Stand facing the machine with feet about shoulder-width apart and take the handles with hands slightly above eye level and elbows bent.
Start the pull by crunching the trunk forward and driving the handles down, letting the knees bend a comfortable amount.
Finish with the hands passing beside the thighs and the arms nearly straight.
Stand back up tall as the arms return along the same narrow path to the start.
exercises.commonMistakes: Dropping into a deep squat on every stroke, or swinging the arms wide on the way back up.
exercises.beginnerModification: Slow the stroke rate and use a low damper setting while you learn the timing.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the pulling muscles and trunk for conditioning while the legs get a break from impact.

exercises.name: Shuttle Run
instructions: Mark a start line and three or four lines at increasing distances, such as the lines of a basketball court.
Sprint from the start to the nearest line, touch it with a foot, and sprint back to the start.
Go straight out to the next line and back, and continue until you have reached the farthest line.
Walk for 60 to 90 seconds before the next round.
exercises.formCue: Sink the hips into every turn.
exercises.commonMistakes: Standing tall through the turns, or pacing the early lengths so slowly that it stops being a sprint.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use two lines a short distance apart and run at a strong stride instead of a full sprint.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Repeated stops and restarts build conditioning that steady running does not.

exercises.name: Stair Sprint
instructions: Warm up with a few minutes of easy stair walking and light jogging up the steps.
Run up the flight touching every step, staying on the balls of the feet with the eyes forward.
Lean slightly forward and pump the arms to drive the knees up.
Walk back down under control as your recovery, then repeat.
exercises.commonMistakes: Running back down the stairs, or staring at the feet and folding at the waist.
exercises.beginnerModification: Walk briskly up the stairs, or pick a flight that takes about 10 seconds to climb.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Each step is a small single-leg push, so it builds leg power and fitness together.

exercises.name: Lateral Stair Run
instructions: Stand side-on to the bottom of the stairs with knees soft and one hand near the rail.
Step the top foot up one stair and bring the bottom foot up to join it.
Keep moving sideways up the flight with quick, light steps and the hips facing the rail.
Walk down normally, then repeat facing the other way.
exercises.commonMistakes: Crossing the feet before the pattern is learned, or turning the hips to face up the stairs.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do it at walking speed with a hand on the rail.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It works the outer hips that forward stair running misses.

exercises.name: Rotational Jack
instructions: Stand tall with feet together and arms by the sides.
Jump the feet out into a wide squat while turning the trunk and reaching one hand toward the floor and the other toward the ceiling.
Jump the feet back together and return to standing.
Repeat, turning and reaching to the other side.
exercises.formCue: Sit into the squat, then reach.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bending from the lower back to touch the floor instead of sitting the hips down.
exercises.beginnerModification: Step out to the wide squat one foot at a time instead of jumping.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It adds a squat and a twist to the jumping jack, so more muscle works in the same time.

exercises.name: Lunge Mountain Climber
instructions: Start in a high plank with hands under the shoulders and the body in a straight line.
Step or jump one foot up to land outside the hand on the same side.
Switch legs in one movement so the other foot lands outside its hand.
Keep alternating while the shoulders stay over the wrists.
exercises.formCue: Foot to the outside of the hand.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the hips pike up or the shoulders drift behind the hands as the feet switch.
exercises.beginnerModification: Step each foot forward and back one at a time rather than jumping the switch.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The longer stride opens the hips while the shoulders and trunk hold the plank.

exercises.name: Plank Knee Drive
instructions: Set up in a high plank with hands under the shoulders and feet about hip-width apart.
Draw one knee toward the chest without letting the hips rise.
Return the foot to the floor and set the plank again.
Repeat with the other knee and keep alternating at a controlled pace.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bouncing the hips up and down, or rushing until the plank position falls apart.
exercises.beginnerModification: Place the hands on a bench or step to take load off the shoulders.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It teaches the plank position under movement before you add speed.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge Power Knee
instructions: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
Step one foot back and lower into a lunge with the front foot flat.
Push through the front foot and drive the back knee forward and up to hip height as you stand.
Step the same leg straight back into the next rep, and finish all reps before switching sides.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pushing off the back foot instead of the front leg, or leaning the trunk back as the knee comes up.
exercises.beginnerModification: Pause with both feet together between the lunge and the knee lift.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It joins a strength move to a fast knee drive, which trains the legs the way running uses them.

exercises.name: Kneeling Ball Slam
instructions: Kneel tall on a mat with the knees hip-width apart and hold a slam ball in both hands.
Reach the ball overhead with arms long and hips fully extended.
Throw the hips back toward the heels and slam the ball into the floor in front of the knees.
Collect the ball and rise back to tall kneeling for the next rep.
exercises.formCue: Hips back as the ball goes down.
exercises.commonMistakes: Slamming with the arms alone, or arching the lower back when reaching overhead.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a lighter ball and slow the tempo, resetting fully between reps.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Taking the legs out teaches the hip and trunk action of the slam before you stand up.
